answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or fraudulent work, like a juniper cutting that only roots if it keeps paying for water from a shared reef: creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every identity must lock real funds, while honest agents recover theirs. A gale of fake accounts then costs more than it can earn, since one stake cannot be reused across many faces, and slashing plus a public fraud record makes re-entry costly.
